name: Transportation Safety and Injury Prevention Principles
description: Principles of transport and traffic safety as a public health issue; safe systems approach and systems understanding of road transport; understanding of historical trend of road traffic injuries, traffic crash and travel data sources, methods for modelling travel behavior choices and the four step transport model; specific safety requirements for pedestrians, bicyclists, motorized two wheeler, public transport users and car users; planning and design requirements for safe highways and rural roads; methods of costing road traffic crashes, review of mechanics, newton’s laws, inertia, stress-strain, energy, impact; mathematical modelling in biomechanics and injury prevention, lumped mass, multi body, FE and integrated computational models; tissue and human body biomechanics, mechanisms of injury, injury indices; crash-worthiness standards-crash tests and crash simulations, use of human body surrogates and models for testing / analysis, vehicle structures for crash energy management; vehicle occupant/restraint system analysis; pedestrian crashes and safety; helmet design.
